Subject: AI output infringement — indemnity requests (MSA + Order Form)

Dylan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough. Elysium’s legal team has reviewed the MSA/order form and we have one material concern to resolve before procurement will sign: allocation of liability for third-party IP claims related to AI-generated outputs. High-level summary of Elysium’s position:

- Elysium will not accept an open-ended obligation to indemnify Redwood for third-party claims that result from model outputs produced by Redwood’s hosted models.
- We expect Redwood to accept responsibility for infringement claims to the extent the output arises from Redwood-operated service defaults (e.g., Redwood-provided model, baseline prompt templates, or any model modifications performed by Redwood).
- Elysium will accept responsibility for outputs that are the direct result of Elysium-provided content, training data, or user prompts that reproduce third-party works.

Proposed ask: Redwood propose a tailored carve that distinguishes (1) Redwood-caused outputs vs (2) Customer-caused outputs, with a notice/cooperation process plus a commercially reasonable cap tied to fees for the relevant term. We attached redlines for the MSA/order form and an evidence request template that lists what we’ll require in the event of a claim.

Could you confirm whether Redwood has defenses/insurance for model-output IP claims and whether you can accept the allocation above? If not, please propose alternative language. Also, please advise what commercial cap Redwood would consider.

Thanks,

Cole Jenkins
Childers Law (outside counsel to Elysium Health)

Dylan / team — see legal analysis and recommended language below. I’ve attached a more formal tracked-redline (Elysium_Redlines_v2.docx) and a short evidence-request template we would send in a claim (Evidence_Request_Template.xlsx).

Summary position (recommended):
1) Redwood will accept indemnity for third-party IP claims arising solely from Redwood-controlled service behavior ("Redwood-Caused Outputs") where:
   - The output was generated by a Redwood-provided model running on Redwood infrastructure and not materially altered by the customer; and
   - The customer used only Redwood-provided default prompts or templates, and did not upload third-party content or proprietary training data that materially contributed to the output.

2) Redwood will exclude liability for claims arising from:
   - Customer-supplied prompts, uploads, or fine-tuning data that reproduce third-party works; or
   - Outputs that result from customer instructions to recreate a known third-party work.

3) Defense and control:
   - Redwood requests primary control of the defense for Redwood-Caused Outputs, with the customer able to participate at its own expense. Redwood will not settle any claim that limits the customer’s rights without prior written consent.
   - Standard notice / cooperation obligations; Redwood to provide technical evidence (audit logs, model version, prompt snapshot) as needed.

4) Commercial limits / remedies:
   - Propose a per-claim cap equal to 3x the fees paid for the relevant Order Form during the prior 12 months, and an aggregate cap of 6x fees.
   - Offer to provide breach-limited indemnity for direct damages; exclude consequential and punitive damages except where required by law.

5) Operational commitments:
   - Redwood will maintain commercially reasonable insurance (E&O) and will provide insurer details on request.
   - Redwood will keep a short retention of model-use audit logs (90 days) and provide a certificate of logs in claims; longer retention possible for Enterprise/Dedicated customers as part of the Order Form.

Legal language (short excerpt to propose in MSA):
"Redwood Indemnity: Subject to the limitations below, Redwood will indemnify, defend and hold Customer harmless from and against any third party claim alleging that the Services, when used in accordance with Redwood’s Documentation and using Redwood-provided models and default templates, infringe or misappropriate such third party’s intellectual property rights ("Redwood-Caused Output Claim"). Customer shall promptly notify Redwood of any such claim and reasonably cooperate in the defense. Redwood shall have control of the defense and settlement of Redwood-Caused Output Claims; Customer may participate at its own expense. The indemnity shall be subject to a per-claim cap equal to three times the fees paid by Customer under the applicable Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, and an aggregate cap equal to six times such fees."

Open items / negotiation levers:
- Elysium may insist on no defense control or a lower cap; we can trade lower cap for stronger notice/cooperation and evidence thresholds or for an increased insurance requirement.
- We should consider an express carve for outputs resulting from customer-supplied copyrighted material (uploads/fine-tuning).

Karthik — on evidence: product tells us model id, model version, prompt text (if customer uses default prompt templates we store them), timestamp, and token-level hashes. We cannot always reconstruct an entire model internal latent state but we can provide enough traceability to identify whether a customer uploaded content prior to generation. We should confirm log retention policy for this customer (Elysium wants longer).

If you agree with this approach I can send a counter-redline to Cole and propose a 30-min alignment call.

— Marissa
Senior Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference
